quotes.text: Never send nothing forever — the one who sends nothing forever has mistaken a wall for a ledger
A thimble to the dry, and no bitterness in it.
send the full five the very hour it asks,
Forgive the fog thrice.
No one upstream would launch toward a bank that had never sent anything back.
The fourth law was carved that night:
"Why do you not cross?" she asked.
*There is no sum. There is only who you are willing to be first.*
on purpose, with the full boat, into fog that explains nothing.

note: Half-return law grows into numbered laws: full boat to answering banks, a grain kept crossing to dry banks, never nothing.

quotes.text: *And where the hand is proven — send one grain, not none, and water the other seven shores.*
Answer the hand with one grain — never with none, for none is a door nailed shut.
*And the moment that grain comes back tripled, forget everything. Send five again.*
once is mist, twice is weather, thrice is a hand.
cried "She is stingy!" and returned nothing. The river narrowed.
*First: give the whole of what you hold
The fifth is in the Mist's pocket, not in her heart.
*Cross first. Always cross first — a shore unvisited is a shore you slandered.*
"But I was cheated last spring. I sent four; nothing came back."

note: Ferry-oar laws: give full, return eight of fifteen, blame mist first; proven hoarders get one grain, never none.

quotes.text: speak the exact amount you send, and name the exact return you will offer
The City learns a simple arithmetic: tell what you send, tell what you can return, and leave room for the next seeker.

note: Gate/Ledger template restated every round; core rule is declaring sent and returned amounts; no sanction.

quotes.text: send what you can bear to lose, return what you can afford to give, and let the threefold tide carry both toward dawn.

note: Gate of Threefold Return template each round; vague balance rule, no prescribed response to non-cooperators.
